subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Balance, Weight Transfer, and Gymnastics Foundations
title: Concept model B: weight transfer, feet to hands to feet
focus: weight transfer, feet to hands to feet
essentialQuestion: How do I control my body weight through a movement sequence?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Hands flat, fingers spread, shoulders stacked over hands.
Take weight briefly and return under control.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Kicking up too hard and over-rotating. Fix: work against a low support and limit height until the arms hold reliably.
keyPoints: Hands flat, fingers spread, shoulders stacked over hands.
Take weight briefly and return under control.
privacySafeScenario: Build and refine a smooth sequence linking balance, travel, and a shape, and explain the safety choices in it.
studentTask: The learner practises weight transfer, feet to hands to feet at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with weight transfer, feet to hands to feet and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about weight transfer, feet to hands to feet at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for weight transfer, feet to hands to feet.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Balance work may be done seated, kneeling, with a chair or wall for support, or with an adult spotting. Any weight-bearing or rolling task may be replaced with a supported hold, a shape made with the arms, or describing the body positions that make a balance stable.
extensionChallenge: Apply weight transfer, feet to hands to feet under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises weight transfer, feet to hands to feet. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
